[NFCT.2.3] Each `ds_slot_value_t.kind` must match the slot's declared
`ds_slot_type_t`. There is **no implicit conversion**; a mismatch is
`DS_ERR_SLOT_TYPE_MISMATCH` (IDAT.4.6):

| Schema slot type | Required value kind | Union member |
|---|---|---|
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_INT`    | `DS_SLOT_INT`      | `v.i` |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_FLOAT`  | `DS_SLOT_FLOAT`    | `v.f` |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_STRING` | `DS_SLOT_STRING`   | `v.s` (non-NULL) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_BOOL`   | `DS_SLOT_BOOL`     | `v.b` |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_JSON`   | `DS_SLOT_JSON`     | `v.json` (non-NULL parsed tree) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_SCHEMA` | `DS_SLOT_FACT_REF` | `v.ref` (a live fact whose schema equals the slot's `schema_ref`) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_BYTES`  | `DS_SLOT_BYTES`    | `v.bytes` (`ds_bytes_view_t` data+len) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_TIME`   | `DS_SLOT_INT`      | `v.i` (UTC nanoseconds, [RDSC.5.5.8]) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_DATE`   | `DS_SLOT_INT`      | `v.i` (epoch days, [RDSC.5.5.8]) |
| `DS_SLOT_TYPE_DURATION` | `DS_SLOT_INT`    | `v.i` (nanoseconds, [RDSC.5.5.8]) |

A negative `v.i` for a `DS_SLOT_TYPE_DURATION` slot is stored as `0`: a
`Duration` is never negative ([LTIM.1.3.1]). That is a value the engine
stores, not a kind it converts, and it is not an error.

A host's reference **must** name a live fact of the slot's `schema_ref`. One that
names a live fact of another schema, or no live fact, is
`DS_ERR_SLOT_TYPE_MISMATCH`, judged at its slot's place in [NFCT.2.11]'s
step 4, on working memory as the call finds it. A `libds.h` caller does not meet
the second: its reference is a handle, and a handle whose fact is not live is
undefined behaviour ([IDAT.1.6]). A runtime whose host names a fact by its id does
meet it, and its engine **must** judge it, because the recording of such an assert
inlines each referenced live fact ([RFCS.24.1]). A target that leaves after the
assert does not undo it: a read of the slot then finds the target gone.
A delivery's references are [RFCS.23.7]'s: it judges them once, on working memory
as the call finds it, and a target the delivery's own asserts remove is this case
too.

This is the host-boundary statement of a working-memory invariant, not a
property of this API: [RARC.5.2.6] binds every path into working memory to the
same rule, so a rule-fired `emit` is held to this table exactly as a host
assertion is.
